newsitem.title: USA: IMP to cut staff, sees significant losses.
newsitem.headline: IMP to cut staff, sees significant losses.

text.p: IMP Inc, a maker of mixed integrated circuits, said Monday it expects to report a significant loss for the second quarter ended in September, due to weaker demand and restructuring charges.
The company said it had cut 89 jobs and is also planning periodic factory shut downs to match production with demand.
A spokesman for the company said the reductions are in addition to the 51 job cuts announced in August.
The company also said it had recently experienced "significant yield losses" on deliveries to a major customer.
"This yield problem has since been corrected, but will adversely impact both revenues and profitability for the quarter," the company said.
In the second quarter of fiscal 1996, IMP reported a profit of $1.1 million or $0.04 a share on revenues of $18.5 million.
IMP said it has decided to cease gate array design and manufacturing activities to focus its resources on other aspects of the company's business.

"This will result in a one time charge, primarily due to inventory write-offs and the establishment of reserves," the company said. "The adverse impact of the one time charges associated with the downsizing activities and the termination of the gate array business, combined with the impact from the yield program, has not been quantified, but is expected to result in a very significant loss for the quarter ending Sept. 30, 1996."
The company also announced that, at the request of a major customer, it canceled development of a custom read-channel device that was to be integrated into one of the customer's new products.

"Although there were no anticipated revenues from this product in fiscal 1997, it had been planned to contribute substantially to revenues in fiscal year 1998," the company warned. "Additionally, the company's results for the forseeable future will be impacted by the continuing slowdown in its business."
Specifically, the company said certain of its major customers have requested delays in delivery schedules and reductions in previously ordered amounts for IMP products."
IMP did not disclose which customer had cancelled development of the read channel device, however the company does receive about 12 percent of its revenues from disk drive maker Iomega Corp.

Joe Besecker of Emerald Research in Lancaster, Pennsylvania said he believed Iomega was the customer IMP referred to in its announcement because Iomega had recently said it was seeking second and third source suppliers rather than because of a lack of orders that Iomega was receiving.
Besecker said IMP was a "quality provider" but Iomega needs to find "world class, bigger capacity" suppliers as it forms relationships with original equipment makers (OEM).
